The petitions were clubbed together and heard on various dates, and the Commission also sought certain additional information, including the joint reconciliation statement (in Petition No.149/MP/2021), indicating the bills, the payments and the deductions made and the balance dues. Later, IA No. 26/2023 (in Petition No. 53/2021) (a) The petition has been filed to adjudicate a purely contractual dispute involving the Petitioner and the Respondents. The Petitioner has made only a pure money claim, which could only be adjudicated by the State Commission or the Arbitral Tribunal, upon a reference being made to that effect. It is the case of the Respondent Discoms that a petition for a money claim by a generator against the State Discoms is not maintainable under Section 79 (1) (f) of the Act. It is a settled proposition of law that a statutory body/ Commission can exercise jurisdiction only to the extent provided by the statute. (a) The Respondents have raised two primary contentions viz., (i) It is the State Commission which exercises the jurisdiction over the disputes involved in the present batch of cases, as the dispute raised allegedly do not fall within the scope of Section 79 (1) (b) & (f); (ii) The disputes involved in the present case have to be transfer the petitions to this Commission. This makes it clear that the Central Commission exercises exclusive jurisdiction over the disputes involving the Petitioner and the Respondents. (f) The generating station of the Petitioner is located in the State of Chhattisgarh, and the Petitioner supplies electricity to the States of Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, while the disputes in the present petition arise out of the supply to the State of Andhra Pradesh. Hence, any or all the disputes arising out of the agreements entered into by the Petitioner fall within the jurisdiction of this Commission. The interpretation of the Respondents that the disputes are amenable to the jurisdiction of the State Commission leads to an arbitrary situation, wherein two or more State Commissions concurrently exercise jurisdiction over a given dispute, which is evidently not envisaged under the provisions of the Act. argued that since there is no issue relating to regulation of tariff in the present case, Section 86(1)(f) of the Act, which provides for the adjudication of disputes between the generating company and licensee, on issues other than disputes relating to the determination/regulation of tariff is applicable. Accordingly, the Respondents have submitted that this Commission lacks jurisdiction to adjudicate the disputes raised by the Petitioner in these petitions. _Per contra_ , the Petitioner has argued that the issues involved in the present batch of petitions, necessarily involve a composite scheme and are related to tariff/regulation of tariff and therefore, this Commission only has the jurisdiction to adjudicate the disputes, falling under sub-clauses (a) to (d) of Section 79(1) of the Act and for any other disputes not restricted to these clauses, the same ought to be referred to arbitration. the Respondents, the Commission may refer all the disputes in the present case to arbitration. Accordingly, the dispute resolution clause under the PPA between the parties 38. The Petitioner, in these petitions, has sought claims under various heads, in terms of its prayers (as quoted), relating to the period from 2017 to 2021, along with the Late Payment Surcharge (LPS). Keeping in view the nature of the disputes, the period, the issues and the amounts involved in these petitions, we find it appropriate, to refer the disputes between the parties, in the present petitions (except Petition No.61/MP/2021) for arbitration, in exercise of our powers under Section 79(1)(f) read with Regulation 49(1) (a) of the CERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023. 39. As mentioned earlier, the Petitioner has filed this petition seeking the reliefs, as extracted in para 7 above. Admittedly, the reliefs sought by the Petitioner are against the termination of the PPA by the Respondents, directions to grant STOA and to take supply of power from the Petitioner, relate to breach of contractual obligations and do not impact the tariff or regulation of tariff of the Petitioner, directly or indirectly. Hence, it can be concluded that the dispute raised in this petition is a non-tariff dispute, which the Commission does not have the jurisdiction to adjudicate under Section 79(1)(f) of the Act, and is mandatorily referable to the arbitration, in terms of the decisions of APTEL/ Hon’ble
